q: The angles of depression of two ships from the top of a light house are 45° and 30° towards east. If the ships are 100 m apart, the height of the light house is
s: Let AB be the light house C and D are two ships whose angles of depression on A are 30° and 45° respectively ∠ACB = ∠XAC = 30° , ∠ADB = ∠YAD = 45° and CD = 100m Let AB =h and CB = x then BC = (100 - x)m $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now in }}\,\Delta ACB, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{AB}}{{CB}} \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \sqrt 3 h ......{\text{(i)}} \\ & {\text{Similarly in }}\,\Delta ADB \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BD}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{h}{{100 - x}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 100 - h \,......{\text{(ii)}} \\ & {\text{From (i) and (ii)}} \\ & \sqrt 3 h = 100 - h \\ & \Rightarrow (\sqrt 3 - 1)h = 100 \\ & h = \frac{{100}}{{\sqrt 3 + 1}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}}{{\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}}{{3 - 1}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}}{2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = 50\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \end{aligned}$$ ∴ height of light house $$= 50\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)m$$

q: If the angles of elevation of a tower from two points distance a and b (a > b) from its foot and in the same straight line from it are 30° and 60°, then the height of the tower is?
s: Let AB be the tower and P and Q are such points that PB = a, QB = b and angles of elevation at P and Q are 30° and 60° respectively $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let }}AB = h \\ & {\text{Now in right }}\Delta APB, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{{\text{Perpendicular}}}}{{{\text{Base}}}} = \frac{{AB}}{{PB}} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{h}{a} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{a}\,...........(i) \\ & {\text{Similarly in right }}\Delta AQB, \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{QB}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{h}{b}\,...........(ii) \\ & {\text{Multiplying (i) and (ii)}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} \times \sqrt 3 = \frac{h}{a} \times \frac{h}{b} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{{h^2}}}{{ab}} \\ & \Rightarrow {h^2} = ab \\ & \Rightarrow h = \sqrt {ab} \\ & \therefore {\text{Height of the tower}} = \sqrt {ab} \end{aligned}$$

s: Let height of pole CD = h and AB = 2h, BD = a M is mid-point of BD $$\therefore DM = MB = \frac{a}{2}$$ $${\text{Let }}\angle CMD = \theta ,$$ $${\text{then }}\angle AMB =$$ $${90^ \circ } - \theta$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now}} \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{CD}}{{DM}} = \frac{h}{{\frac{a}{2}}} = \frac{{2h}}{a}\,......({\text{i}}) \\ & {\text{and}} \\ & tan\left( {{{90}^ \circ } - \theta } \right) = \frac{{AB}}{{MB}} = \frac{{2h}}{{\frac{a}{2}}} = \frac{{4h}}{a} \\ & \Rightarrow \cot \theta = \frac{{4h}}{a}\,..........({\text{ii}}) \\ & {\text{Multiplying (i) and (ii)}} \\ & {\text{tan}}\theta \times {\text{cot}}\theta = \frac{{2h}}{a} \times \frac{{4h}}{a} \\ & 1 = \frac{{8{h^2}}}{{{a^2}}} = {h^2} = \frac{{{a^2}}}{8}\,m \\ & h = \sqrt {\frac{{{a^2}}}{8}} = \frac{a}{{\sqrt 8 }} = \frac{a}{{2\sqrt 2 }}\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The tops of two poles of height 20 m and 14 m are connected by a wire. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with horizontal, then the length of the wire is
s: Let AB and CD be two poles AB = 20 m, CD = 14 m A and C are joined by a wire CE || DB and angle of elevation of A is 30° Let CE = DB = x and AC = L Now AE = AB - EB = AB - CD = 20 - 14 = 6 m $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now in right }}\Delta ACE, \\ & \sin \theta = \frac{{{\text{Perpendicular}}}}{{{\text{Hypotenuse}}}} = \frac{{AE}}{{AC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin {30^ \circ } = \frac{6}{{AC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} = \frac{6}{{AC}} \\ & \Rightarrow AC = 2 \times 6 = 12 \\ & \therefore {\text{Length of AC}} = 12\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: A lower subtends an angle of 30° at a point on the same level as its foot. At a second point h metres above the first, the depression of the foot of the tower is 60°. The height of the tower is
s: Let CD is the tower and A is a point such that the angle of elevation of C is 30° B is and their point h m high of A and angle of depression of D is 60° $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{The}}\,AB = h\,m \\ & {\text{Let}}\,CD = H\,m\,\,\,{\text{and }}\,AD\, = x \\ & {\text{Now}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABD, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{AB}}{{AD}} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{h}{{\sqrt 3 }}\,.......({\text{i}}) \\ & {\text{Similarly in right }}\Delta ACB, \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{CD}}{{AD}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{H}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \sqrt 3 \,H\,.......\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,\left( {\text{i}} \right)\,{\text{and}}\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & \sqrt 3 \,H = \frac{h}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & H = \frac{h}{{\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{3} \\ & \therefore {\text{Height of tower}} = \frac{h}{3} \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of depression of a car parked on the road from the top of a 150 m high tower is 30°. The distance of the car from the tower (in metres) is
s: Let AB be the tower of height 150 m C is car and angle of depression is 30° Therefore, ∠ACB = 30° (alternate angle) In right - angled triangle ABC, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{BC}}{{AB}} = \cot {30^ \circ } \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{BC}}{{150}} = \sqrt 3 \\ & \Rightarrow BC = 150\sqrt 3 \,m \end{aligned}$$ That is, distance of the car from the tower is $$150\sqrt 3 \,m$$

q: If the altitude of the sun is at 60°, then the height of the vertical tower that will cast a shadow of length 30 m is
s: Let AB be tower and a point P distance of 30 m from its foot of the tower which form an angle of elevation pf the sun of 60° $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let height of tower }}AB = h \\ & {\text{Then in right }}\Delta APB, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{{\text{Perpendicular}}}}{{{\text{Base}}}} = \frac{{AB}}{{PB}} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{h}{{30}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{h}{{30}} \\ & \Rightarrow h = 30\sqrt 3 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Height of the tower $$= 30\sqrt 3 \,m$$

q: The tops of two poles of height 16 m and 10 m are connected by a wire of length l metres. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, then l =
s: Let AB and CD are two poles AB = 10 m and CD = 16 m AC is wire which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal Let BD = x, then AE = x CE = CD - ED = CD - AB = 16 - 10 = 6m $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now}}\,{\text{in}}\,\Delta ACE \\ & \sin {30^ \circ } = \frac{{CE}}{{AC}} = \frac{6}{l} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} = \frac{6}{l} \\ & \Rightarrow l = 2 \times 6 = 12\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The height of a tower is 100 m. When the angle of elevation of the sun changes from 30° to 45°, the shadow of the tower becomes x metres less. The value of x is
s: Let AB be tower and AB = 100 m and angles of elevation of A at C and D are 30° and 45° respectively and CD = x Let BD = y $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now in right }}\Delta ADB, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{{\text{Perpendicular}}}}{{{\text{Base}}}} = \frac{{AB}}{{DB}} \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{100}}{y} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{100}}{y} \\ & \Rightarrow y = 100 \\ & {\text{Similarly in right }}\Delta ACB, \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{CB}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{100}}{{y + x}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{100}}{{100 + x}} \\ & \Rightarrow 100 + x = 100\sqrt 3 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 100\sqrt 3 - 100 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower standing on a horizontal plane from a point A is α. After walking a distance 'd' towards the foot of the tower the angle of elevation is found to be β. The height of the tower is
s: Let AB be the tower and C is a point such that the angle of elevation of A is α. After walking towards the foot B of the tower, at D the angle of elevation is β. Let h be the height of the tower and DB = x Now in ∆ACB, $$\begin{aligned} & \tan \theta = \frac{{{\text{Perpendicular}}}}{{{\text{Base}}}} = \frac{{AB}}{{CB}} \\ & \tan \alpha = \frac{h}{{d + x}} \\ & \Rightarrow d + x = \frac{h}{{\tan \alpha }} \\ & \Rightarrow d + x = h\cot \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow x = h\cot \alpha - d\,.......\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{Similarly in right }}\Delta ADB, \\ & \tan \beta = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{h}{{\tan \beta }} \\ & \Rightarrow x = h\cot \beta \,.........({\text{ii}}) \\ & {\text{From}}\,\left( {\text{i}} \right)\,{\text{and}}\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & h\cot \alpha - d = h\cot \beta \\ & \Rightarrow h\cot \alpha - h\cot \beta = d \\ & \Rightarrow h\left( {\cot \alpha - \cot \beta } \right) = d \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{d}{{\cot \alpha - \cot \beta }} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Height of the tower $$= \frac{d}{{\cot \alpha - \cot \beta }}$$

q: The length of shadow of a tower on the plane ground is $$\sqrt 3$$ times the height of the tower. The angle of elevation of sun is
s: Let AB be tower and BC be its shadow ∴ Let AB = x $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Then}}\,BC = \sqrt 3 \times x = \sqrt 3 \,x \\ & \therefore \tan \theta = \frac{{AB}}{{BC}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{x}{{\sqrt 3 \,x}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \tan {30^ \circ } \\ & \therefore \theta = {30^ \circ } \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Angle of elevation of the sun$${\text{ = }}{30^ \circ }$$

q: The length of the shadow of a tower standing on level ground is found to 2x meter longer when the sun’s elevation is 30° than when it was 45 °. The height of the tower in meters is
s: AB is a tower BD and BC are its shadows and CD = 2x $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{DB}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{h}{y} \Rightarrow y = h \\ & {\text{and}}\tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{CB}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{{2x + y}} \\ & \Rightarrow 2x + y = \sqrt 3 \,h \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 \,h - h = 2x \\ & \Rightarrow h\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) = 2x \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{2x}}{{\sqrt 3 - 1}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{2x\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}}{{\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{2x\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}}{{3 - 1}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{2x\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}}{2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = x\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right) \end{aligned}$$

q: If the angle of elevation of the top of a tower from two points distant a and b from the base and in the same straight line with It are complementary, then the height of the tower is
s: Let AB be the tower and P and Q are two points such that PB = a and QB = b and angles of elevation are $$\theta$$ and (90° – $$\theta$$) Let height of tower = h $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Then}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta APB, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{{\text{Perpendicular}}}}{{{\text{Base}}}} = \frac{{AB}}{{PB}} \\ & = \frac{h}{a}\,............\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{Similarly in right }}\Delta AQB, \\ & \tan \left( {{{90}^ \circ } - \theta } \right) = \frac{{AB}}{{QB}} = \frac{h}{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \cot \theta = \frac{h}{b}\,...........\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{Multiplying }}\left( {\text{i}} \right){\text{ and }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & \tan \theta \cot \theta = \frac{h}{a} \times \frac{h}{b} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{{h^2}}}{{ab}} \\ & \Rightarrow {h^2} = ab \\ & \Rightarrow h = \sqrt {ab} \\ & \therefore {\text{Height}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{tower}} = \sqrt {ab} \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of the top of a lighthouse 60 m high, from two points on the ground on its opposite sides are 45° and 60°. What is the distance between these two points?
s: Let BD be the lighthouse and A and C be the two points on ground. Then, BD, the height of the lighthouse = 60 m ∠BAD = 45°, ∠BCD = 60° $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BA}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{60}}{{BA}} \\ & \Rightarrow BA = 60\,m\,........\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{{60}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow BC = \frac{{60}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{60 \times \sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{60\sqrt 3 }}{3} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 20\sqrt 3 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 20 \times 1.73 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 34.6\,m\,..........\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \end{aligned}$$ Distance between the two points A and C = AC = BA + BC = 60 + 34.6 [n Substituted value of BA and BC from (i) and (ii)] = 94.6 m

q: On the same side of a tower, two objects are located. Observed from the top of the tower, their angles of depression are 45° and 60°. If the height of the tower is 600 m, the distance between the objects is approximately equal to :
s: Let DC be the tower and A and B be the objects as shown above. Given that DC = 600 m, ∠DAC = 45°, ∠DBC = 60° $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{DC}}{{BC}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{600}}{{BC}} \\ & BC = \frac{{600}}{{\sqrt 3 }}\,..........\,\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{DC}}{{AC}} \\ & 1 = \frac{{600}}{{AC}} \\ & AC = 600\,............\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \end{aligned}$$ Distance between the objects $$= AC = \left( {AC - BC} \right)$$ $$= 600 - \frac{{600}}{{\sqrt 3 }}$$ [n from (1) and (ii)] $$\begin{aligned} & = 600\left( {1 - \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right) \\ & = 600\left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right) \\ & = 600\left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right) \times \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = \frac{{600\sqrt 3 \left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}}{3} \\ & = 200\sqrt 3 \left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \\ & = 200\left( {3 - \sqrt 3 } \right) \\ & = 200\left( {3 - 1.73} \right) \\ & = 254\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: Two ships are sailing in the sea on the two sides of a lighthouse. The angle of elevation of the top of the lighthouse is observed from the ships are 30º and 45º respectively. If the lighthouse is 200 m high, the distance between the two ships is:
s: Let BD be the lighthouse and A and C be the positions of the ships. Then, BD = 200 m, ∠BAD = 30°, ∠BCD = 45° $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BA}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{200}}{{BA}} \\ & \Rightarrow BA = 200\sqrt 3 \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{200}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow BC = 200 \end{aligned}$$ Distance between the two ships $$\begin{aligned} & = AC = BA + BC \\ & = 200\sqrt 3 + 200 \\ & = 200(\sqrt 3 + 1) \\ & = 200\left( {1.73 + 1} \right) \\ & = 200 \times 2.73 \\ & = 546{\text{ }}m \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a certain point is 30°. If the observer moves 40 m towards the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower increases by 15°. The height of the tower is:
s: Let DC be the tower and A and B be the positions of the observer such that AB = 40 m We have ∠DAC = 30°, ∠DBC = 45° Let DC = h $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{DC}}{{AC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{{AC}} \\ & \Rightarrow AC = h\sqrt 3 \,.........\,\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{DC}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{h}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow BC = h\,........\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{We know that,}} \\ & AB = \left( {AC - BC} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 40 = \left( {AC - BC} \right) \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow 40 = \left( {h\sqrt 3 - h} \right)$$ [n from (1) and (ii)] $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 40 = h\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{40}}{{\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{40}}{{\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}} \times \frac{{\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}}{{\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{40\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}}{{\left( {3 - 1} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{40\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right)}}{2} \\ & = 20\left( {\sqrt 3 + 1} \right) \\ & = 20\left( {1.73 + 1} \right) \\ & = 20 \times 2.73 \\ & = 54.6\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of a ladder leaning against a wall is 60º and the foot of the ladder is 12.4 m away from the wall. The length of the ladder is:
s: Consider the diagram shown above where PR represents the ladder and RQ represents the wall. $$\begin{aligned} & \cos {60^ \circ } = \frac{{PQ}}{{PR}} \\ & \frac{1}{2} = \frac{{12.4}}{{PR}} \\ & PR = 2 \times 12.4 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 24.8\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the angle of elevation of the sun when the shadow of a pole of 18 m height is $$6\sqrt 3$$ m long?
s: Let RQ be the pole and PQ be the shadow Given that RQ = 18 m and PQ = $$6\sqrt 3$$ m Let the angle of elevation, ∠RPQ = $$\theta$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From the right}}\Delta PQR, \\ & {\text{tan}}\,\theta = \frac{{RQ}}{{PQ}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{18}}{{6\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{3}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt 3 \\ & \Rightarrow \theta = {\tan ^{ - 1}}\left( {\sqrt 3 } \right) = {60^ \circ } \end{aligned}$$

q: A balloon leaves the earth at a point A and rises vertically at uniform speed. At the end of 2 minutes, John finds the angular elevation of the balloon as 60°. If the point at which John is standing is 150 m away from point A, what is the speed of the balloon?
s: Let C be the position of John. Let A be the position at which balloon leaves the earth and B be the position of the balloon after 2 minutes. Given that CA = 150 m, ∠BCA = 60° $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{BA}}{{CA}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{BA}}{{150}} \\ & BA = 150\sqrt 3 \end{aligned}$$ i.e, the distance travelled by the balloon = $$150\sqrt 3$$ meters time taken = 2 min = 2 × 60 = 120 seconds $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = \frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Time}}}} \\ & = \frac{{150\sqrt 3 }}{{120}} = 1.25\sqrt 3 \end{aligned}$$ = 1.25 × 1.73 = 2.16 meter/second

q: An observer 2 m tall is $$10\sqrt 3$$ m away from a tower. The angle of elevation from his eye to the top of the tower is 30º. The height of the tower is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & SR = PQ = 2\,m \\ & PS = QR = 10\sqrt 3 \,m \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{TS}}{{PS}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{TS}}{{10\sqrt 3 }} \\ & TS = \frac{{10\sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 }} = 10\,m \\ & TR = TS + SR = 10 + 2 = 12\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: A person, standing exactly midway between two towers, observes the top of the two towers at angle of elevation of 22.5° and 67.5°. What is the ratio of the height of the taller tower to the height of the shorter tower? (Given that tan 22.5° = $$\sqrt 2 - 1$$ )
s: Let ED be the taller tower and AB be the shorter tower. Let C be the point of observation Given that ∠ ACB = 22.5° and ∠ DCE = 67.5° Given that C is the midpoint of BD Hence, BC = CD $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,ABC, \\ & \tan{22.5^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BC}}\,.....\left( {eq:1} \right)\, \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,CDE, \\ & \tan {67.5^ \circ } = \frac{{ED}}{{CD}}\,.....\left( {eq:2} \right) \\ & \frac{{\left( {eq:2} \right)}}{{\left( {eq:1} \right)}} \Rightarrow \frac{{\tan {{67.5}^ \circ }}}{{\tan{{22.5}^ \circ }}} = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{ED}}{{CD}}} \right)}}{{\left( {\frac{{AB}}{{BC}}\,} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{ED}}{{AB}}\,\,\,\,\,\left( {\because CD = BC} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\tan \left( {{{90}^ \circ } - {{22.5}^ \circ }} \right)}}{{\tan {{22.5}^ \circ }}} = \frac{{ED}}{{AB}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\cot {{22.5}^ \circ }}}{{\tan {{22.5}^ \circ }}} = \frac{{ED}}{{AB}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left[ {\because \tan \left( {90 - \theta } \right) = \cot \theta } \right] \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\left( {\frac{1}{{\tan {{22.5}^ \circ }}}} \right)}}{{\tan {{22.5}^ \circ }}} = \frac{{ED}}{{AB}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left[ {\because \cot \theta = \frac{1}{{\tan \theta }}} \right] \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ED}}{{AB}} = \frac{1}{{{{\left( {\tan {{22.5}^ \circ }} \right)}^2}}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{{{\left( {\sqrt 2 - 1} \right)}^2}}} \\ & = {\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 - 1}}} \right)^2} \\ & = {\left[ {\frac{{\left( {\sqrt 2 + 1} \right)}}{{\left( {\sqrt 2 - 1} \right)\left( {\sqrt 2 + 1} \right)}}} \right]^2} \\ & = {\left[ {\frac{{\left( {\sqrt 2 + 1} \right)}}{{\left( {2 - 1} \right)}}} \right]^2} \\ & = {\left[ {\frac{{\left( {\sqrt 2 + 1} \right)}}{1}} \right]^2} \\ & = {\left( {\sqrt 2 + 1} \right)^2} \\ & = \left( {2 + 2\sqrt 2 + 1} \right) \\ & = \left( {3 + 2\sqrt 2 } \right) \\ & {\text{Required}}\,{\text{Ratio}} \\ & = ED:AB \\ & = \left( {3 + 2\sqrt 2 } \right):1 \end{aligned}$$

q: A vertical tower stands on ground and is surmounted by a vertical flagpole of height 18 m. At a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the bottom and the top of the flagpole are 30° and 60° respectively. What is the height of the tower?
s: Let DC be the vertical tower and AD be the vertical flagpole. Let B be the point of observation. Given that AD = 18 m, ∠ ABC = 60°, ∠ DBC = 30° Let DC be h $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{DC}}{{BC}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{{BC}} \\ & h = \frac{{BC}}{{\sqrt 3 }}\,......\left( eq : 1 \right) \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{AC}}{{BC}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{18 + h}}{{BC}} \\ & 18 + h = BC \times \sqrt 3 \,......\left( eq: 2 \right) \\ & \frac{eq : 1}{eq : 2} \Rightarrow \frac{h}{{18 + h}} = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{BC}}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)}}{{\left( {BC \times \sqrt 3 } \right)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{1}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow 3h = 18 + h \\ & \Rightarrow 2h = 18 \\ & \Rightarrow h = 9\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e., the height of the tower = 9 m

q: To a man standing outside his house, the angles of elevation of the top and bottom of a window are 60° and 45° respectively. If the height of the man is 180 cm and he is 5 m away from the wall, what is the length of the window?
s: Let AB be the man and CD be the window Given that the height of the man, AB = 180 cm, the distance between the man and the wall, BE = 5 m, ∠ DAF = 45°, ∠ CAF = 60° From the diagram, AF = BE = 5 m $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,AFD, \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{DF}}{{AF}} \\ & 1 = \frac{{DF}}{5} \\ & DF = 5\,......\left( 1 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,AFC, \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{CF}}{{AF}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{CF}}{5} \\ & CF = 5\sqrt 3 \,......\,\left( 2 \right) \\ & {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{window}} \\ & = CD = \left( {CF - DF} \right) \end{aligned}$$ $$= 5\sqrt 3 - 5$$ [n Substituted the value of CF and DF from (1) and (2)] $$\begin{aligned} & = 5\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \\ & = 5\left( {1.73 - 1} \right) \\ & = 5 \times 0.73 \\ & = 3.65\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: When the sun's altitude changes from 30° to 60°, the length of the shadow of a tower decreases by 70m. What is the height of the tower?
s: Let AD be the tower, BD be the initial shadow and CD be the final shadow. Given that BC = 70 m, ∠ ABD = 30°, ∠ ACD = 60°, Let CD = x, AD = h $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,CDA \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{AD}}{{CD}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{h}{x}\,......\left( {eq:1} \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,BDA \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AD}}{{BD}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{{70 + x}}\,......\left( {eq:2} \right) \\ & \frac{{eq:1}}{{eq:2}} \Rightarrow \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{{\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)}} = \frac{{\left( {\frac{h}{x}} \right)}}{{\left( {\frac{h}{{70 + x}}} \right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow 3 = \frac{{70 + x}}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 70 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 35 \end{aligned}$$ Substituting this value of x in eq : 1, we have $$\begin{aligned} & \sqrt 3 = \frac{h}{{35}} \\ & \Rightarrow h = 35\sqrt 3 = 35 \times 1.73 \\ & = 60.55 \approx 60.6 \end{aligned}$$

q: From a point P on a level ground, the angle of elevation of the top tower is 30º. If the tower is 200 m high, the distance of point P from the foot of the tower is:
The angles of depression and elevation of the top of a wall 11 m high from top and bottom of a tree are 60° and 30° respectively. What is the height of the tree?
s: Let DC be the wall, AB be the tree. Given that ∠DBC = 30°, ∠DAE = 60°, DC = 11 m $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{DC}}{{BC}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{11}}{{BC}} \\ & BC = 11\sqrt 3 \,m \\ & AE = BC = 11\sqrt 3 \,m\,.....\left( 1 \right) \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{ED}}{{AE}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\sqrt 3 = \frac{{ED}}{{11\sqrt 3 }}$$ [n Substituted value of AE from (1)] $$\begin{aligned} & ED = 11\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 11 \times 3 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 33 \\ & {\text{Height}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{tree}} \\ & = AB = EC = \left( {ED + DC} \right) \\ & = 33 + 11 \\ & = 44\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of the top of the tower from a point on the ground is $${\sin ^{ - 1}}\left({\frac{3}{5}} \right).$$ If the point of observation is 20 meters away from the foot of the tower, what is the height of the tower?
s: Consider a right-angled triangle PQR as shown below. Let QR = 3 and PR = 5 such that $$\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}\,\,\,\,\left[ {{\text{i}}{\text{.e}}{\text{.}},\theta = {{\sin }^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{3}{5}} \right)} \right]$$ $$PQ = \sqrt {P{R^2} - Q{R^2}}$$ (n Pythagorean theorem) $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {{5^2} - {3^2}} \\ & = 4 \end{aligned}$$ $${\text{i}}{\text{.e}}{\text{.}},\,{\text{when}}\,\theta = {\sin ^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{3}{5}} \right),$$ PQ : QR = 4 : 3 ......(eq : 1) Now Let's solve the question. Let P be the point of observation and QR be the tower as shown in the below diagram. $${\text{Given}}\,{\text{that}}\,\theta = {\sin ^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{3}{5}} \right)$$ and PQ = 20 m We know that PQ : QR = 4 : 3 (from eq : 1) $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{i}}{\text{.e}}{\text{.}},\,20:QR = 4:3 \\ & \Rightarrow 20 \times 3 = QR \times 4 \\ & \Rightarrow QR = 15\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e. height of the tower = 15 m Solution 2 Let P be the point of observation and QR be the tower. $${\text{Given}}\,{\text{that}}\,\theta = {\sin ^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{3}{5}} \right)$$ and PQ = 20 m Let the height of the tower, QR = h and PR = x $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta PQR, \\ & \sin \theta = \frac{{QR}}{{PR}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \left[ {{{\sin }^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{3}{5}} \right)} \right] = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{3}{5} = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{5h}}{3}\,.....\left( {eq:1} \right) \end{aligned}$$ From Pythagorean theorem, we have $$\begin{aligned} & P{Q^2} + Q{R^2} = P{R^2} \\ & {20^2} + {h^2} = {x^2} \end{aligned}$$ $${20^2} + {h^2} = {\left( {\frac{{5h}}{3}} \right)^2}$$ (n Substituted the value of x from eq:1) $$\begin{aligned} & {20^2} + {h^2} = \frac{{25{h^2}}}{9} \\ & \frac{{16{h^2}}}{9} = {20^2} \\ & \frac{{4h}}{3} = 20 \\ & h = \frac{{3 \times 20}}{4} = 15{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e. height of the tower = 15 m

q: A ladder 10 m long just reaches the top of a wall and makes an angle of 60° with the wall.Find the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall $$\left( {\sqrt 3 = 1.73} \right)$$
s: Let BA be the ladder and AC be the wall as shown above. Then the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall = BC Given that BA = 10 m, ∠ BAC = 60° $$\begin{aligned} & \sin {60^ \circ } = \frac{{BC}}{{BA}} \\ & \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} = \frac{{BC}}{{10}} \\ & BC = 10 \times \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 5 \times 1.73 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 8.65\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A man standing at a point P is watching the top of a tower, which makes an angle of elevation of 30º with the man's eye. The man walks some distance towards the tower to watch its top and the angle of the elevation becomes 45º. What is the distance between the base of the tower and the point P?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{SR}}{{QR}} \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{SR}}{{PR}} = \frac{{SR}}{{\left( {PQ + QR} \right)}} \end{aligned}$$ Two equations and 3 variables. Hence we can not find the required value with the given data. (Note that if one of SR, PQ, QR is known, this becomes two equations and two variables and if that was the case, we could have found out the required value.)

q: A vertical pole fixed to the ground is divided in the ratio 1 : 9 by a mark on it with lower part shorter than the upper part. If the two parts subtend equal angles at a place on the ground, 15 m away from the base of the pole, what is the height of the pole?
s: Let CB be the pole and point D divides it such that BD : DC = 1 : 9 Given that AB = 15 m Let the the two parts subtend equal angles at point A such that ∠ CAD = ∠ BAD = $$\theta$$ From "Angle Bisector Theorem", we have $$\frac{{BD}}{{DC}} = \frac{{AB}}{{AC}}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{9} = \frac{{15}}{{AC}}$$ [n BD : DC = 1 : 9 and AB = 15(given)] $$\Rightarrow AC = 15 \times 9\,{\text{m}}\,......\left( {eq:1} \right)$$ $${\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABC,$$ $$CB = \sqrt {A{C^2} - A{B^2}}$$ (n Pythagorean theorem) $$= \sqrt {{{\left( {15 \times 9} \right)}^2} - {{15}^2}}$$ [nAC=15 × 9(eq : 1) and AB=15 m(given)] $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {{{15}^2} \times {9^2} - {{15}^2}} \\ & = \sqrt {{{15}^2}\left( {{9^2} - 1} \right)} \\ & = \sqrt {{{15}^2} \times 80} \\ & = \sqrt {{{15}^2} \times 16 \times 5} \\ & = 15 \times 4 \times \sqrt 5 \\ & = 60\sqrt 5 \,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A man is watching from the top of a tower a boat speeding away from the tower. The boat makes an angle of depression of 45° with the man's eye when at a distance of 100 metres from the tower. After 10 seconds, the angle of depression becomes 30°. What is the approximate speed of the boat, assuming that it is running in still water?
s: Consider the diagram shown above. Let AB be the tower. Let C and D be the positions of the boat Then, ∠ ACB = 45°, ∠ ADC = 30°, BC = 100 m $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{AB}}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow AB = 100\,......\left( {eq:1} \right) \end{aligned}$$ $$\tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BD}}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{100}}{{BD}}$$ (n Substituted the value of AB from equation 1) $$\Rightarrow BD = 100\sqrt 3$$ $$\begin{aligned} & CD = \left( {BD - BC} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {100\sqrt 3 - 100} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \end{aligned}$$ It is given that the distance CD is covered in 10 seconds. i.e., the distance $$100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)$$ is covered in 10 seconds. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Required}}\,{\text{speed}} \\ & = \frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Time}}}} \\ & = \frac{{100\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}}{{10}} \\ & = 10\left( {1.73 - 1} \right) \\ & = 7.3\,{\text{meter/seconds}} \\ & = 7.3 \times \frac{{18}}{5}\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 26.28\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: An aeroplane when 900 m high passes vertically above another aeroplane at an instant when their angles of elevation at same observing point are 60° and 45° respectively. Approximately, how many meters higher is the one than the other?
s: Let C and D be the position of the aeroplanes. Given that CB = 900 m, ∠ CAB = 60°, ∠ DAB = 45° $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABC, \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{CB}}{{AB}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{900}}{{AB}} \\ & AB = \frac{{900}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{900 \times \sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{900\sqrt 3 }}{3} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 300\sqrt 3 \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABD, \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{DB}}{{AB}} \\ & 1 = \frac{{DB}}{{AB}} \\ & DB = AB = 300\sqrt 3 \\ & \\ & {\text{Required}}\,{\text{height}} \\ & = CD \\ & = \left( {CB - DB} \right) \\ & = \left( {900 - 300\sqrt 3 } \right) \\ & = \left( {900 - 300 \times 1.73} \right) \\ & = \left( {900 - 519} \right) \\ & = 381\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of the sun, when the length of the shadow of a tree is equal to the height of the tree, is:
s: Consider the diagram shown above where QR represents the tree and PQ represents its shadow $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{We}}\,{\text{have}},\,QR = PQ \\ & {\text{Let}}\,\angle QPR = \theta \end{aligned}$$ $$\tan \theta = \frac{{QR}}{{PQ}} = 1$$ (since QR = PQ) $$\Rightarrow \theta = {45^ \circ }$$ i.e., required angle of elevation = 45°

q: Two persons are on either sides of a tower of height 50 m. The persons observers the top of the tower at an angle of elevation of 30° and 60°. If a car crosses these two persons in 10 seconds, what is the speed of the car?
s: Let BD be the tower and A and C be the positions of the persons. Given that BD = 50 m, ∠ BAD = 30°, ∠ BCD = 60° $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta \,ABD, \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BA}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{50}}{{BA}} \\ & \Rightarrow BA = 50\sqrt 3 \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta CBD, \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{{50}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow BC = \frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50 \times \sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50\sqrt 3 }}{3} \end{aligned}$$ Distance between the two persons $$\begin{aligned} & = AC = BA + BC \\ & = 50\sqrt 3 + \frac{{50\sqrt 3 }}{3} \\ & = \sqrt 3 \left( {50 + \frac{{50}}{3}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{200\sqrt 3 }}{3}\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e., the distance travelled by the car in 10 seconds = $$\frac{{200\sqrt 3 }}{3}\,{\text{m}}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of the car}} = \frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Time}}}} \\ & = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{200\sqrt 3 }}{3}} \right)}}{{10}} = \frac{{200\sqrt 3 }}{3}\,{\text{m/s}} \\ & = \frac{{200\sqrt 3 }}{3} \times \frac{{18}}{5}\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = {\text{24}}\sqrt 3 \,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A man on the top of a vertical observation tower observers a car moving at a uniform speed coming directly towards it. If it takes 8 minutes for the angle of depression to change from 30° to 45°, how soon after this will the car reach the observation tower?
s: Consider the diagram shown above. Let AB be the tower. Let D and C be the positions of the car. Then, ∠ ADC = 30° , ∠ ACB = 45° Let AB = h, BC = x, CD = y $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BC}} = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{h}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow h = x\,......\left( 1 \right) \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BD}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{AB}}{{\left( {BC + CD} \right)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{h}{{x + y}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{h}{{x + y}} \\ & \Rightarrow x + y = \sqrt 3 \,h \\ & \Rightarrow y = \sqrt 3 \,h - x \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow y = \sqrt 3 \,h - h$$ (n Substituted the value of x from equation 1 ) $$\Rightarrow y = h\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)$$ Given that distance y is covered in 8 minutes. i.e, distance $$h\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)$$ is covered in 8 minutes. Time to travel distance x = Time to travel distance h (n Since x = h as per equation 1). Let distance h is covered in t minutes. since distance is proportional to the time when the speed is constant, we have $$\begin{aligned} & h\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \propto 8\,......\left( {\text{A}} \right) \\ & h \propto t\,..............\left( {\text{B}} \right) \\ & \frac{{\left( {\text{A}} \right)}}{{\left( {\text{B}} \right)}} \Rightarrow \frac{{h\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}}{h} = \frac{8}{t} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) = \frac{8}{t} \\ & \Rightarrow t = \frac{8}{{\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{8}{{\left( {1.73 - 1} \right)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{8}{{.73}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{800}}{{73}}\,{\text{minutes}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 10\frac{{70}}{{73}}\,{\text{minutes}} \\ & \approx {\text{10}}\,{\text{minutes}}\,{\text{57}}\,{\text{seconds}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two vertical poles are 200 m apart and the height of one is double that of the other. From the middle point of the line joining their feet, an observer finds the angular elevations of their tops to be complementary. Find the heights of the poles.
s: Let AB and CD be the poles with heights h and 2h respectively. Given that distance between the poles, BD = 200 m Let E be the middle point of BD, ∠ AEB = $$\theta$$ ∠ CED = (90 - $$\theta$$) (n given that angular elevations are complementary) Since E is the middle point of BD, we have BE = ED = 100 m $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABE, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{AB}}{{BE}} \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{h}{{100}} \\ & h = 100\tan \theta \,......\left( 1 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta EDC, \\ & \tan\left( {90 - \theta } \right) = \frac{{CD}}{{ED}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\cot \theta = \frac{{2h}}{{100}}$$ $$\left[ {\because \tan \left( {90 - \theta } \right) = \cot \theta } \right]$$ $$\begin{aligned} & 2h = 100\cot \theta \,......\left( 2 \right) \\ & \left( 1 \right) \times \left( 2 \right) \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow 2{h^2} = {100^2}$$ $$\left[ {\because \tan \theta \times \cot\theta = \tan\theta \times \frac{1}{{\tan \theta }} = 1} \right]$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sqrt 2 \,h = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{100}}{{\sqrt 2 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{100 \times \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 2 \times \sqrt 2 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 50\sqrt 2 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 50 \times 1.41 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 70.5 \\ & \Rightarrow 2h = 2 \times 70.5 = 141 \end{aligned}$$ i.e. the height of the poles are 70.5 m and 141 m.

q: From the foot and the top of a building of height 230 m, a person observes the top of a tower with angles of elevation of b and a respectively. What is the distance between the top of these buildings if tan a = $$\frac{5}{{12}}$$ and tan b = $$\frac{4}{{5}}$$
s: Let ED be the building and AC be the tower. Given that ED = 230 m, ∠ADC = b, ∠AEB = a Also given that tan a = $$\frac{5}{{12}}$$ and tan b = $$\frac{4}{{5}}$$ Let AC = h Required Distance = Distance between the top of these buildings = AE $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABE, \\ & \tan \left( a \right) = \frac{{AB}}{{BE}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{5}{{12}} = \frac{{\left( {h - 230} \right)}}{{BE}}$$ [n tan(a) = $$\frac{5}{{12}}$$ (given), AB = (AC - BC) = (AC - ED) = (h - 230)] $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow BE = \frac{{12\left( {h - 230} \right)}}{5}\,.....\left( 1 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ACD, \\ & \tan \left( b \right) = \frac{{AC}}{{CD}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{4}{5} = \frac{h}{{CD}}$$ [n tan(b) = $$\frac{4}{5}$$ (given), AC = h] $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow CD = \frac{{5h}}{4}\,.....\left( 2 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{diagram,}}\,BE = CD \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{{12\left( {h - 230} \right)}}{5} = \frac{{5h}}{4}$$ (from equation 1 & 2) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 48h - \left( {4 \times 12 \times 230} \right) = 25h \\ & \Rightarrow 23h = \left( {4 \times 12 \times 230} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{\left( {4 \times 12 \times 230} \right)}}{{23}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 480\,{\text{m}}\,......\left( 3 \right) \\ & AB = \left( {AC - BC} \right) \end{aligned}$$ $$\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {480 - 230} \right)$$ [n Since AC = h = 480 (from 3) and BC = ED = 230 m(given)] $$\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 250\,{\text{m}}$$ In the triangle ABE, tan(a) =$$\frac{5}{{12}}$$ . Let's figure out the value of sin(a) now. Consider a triangle with opposite side = 5 and adjacent side = 12 such that tan(a) = $$\frac{5}{{12}}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{hypotenuse}} = \sqrt {{5^2} + {{12}^2}} = 13 \\ & {\text{i}}{\text{.e}}{\text{.,}} \\ & \sin \left( a \right) = \frac{{{\text{opposite}}\,{\text{side}}}}{{{\text{hypotenuse}}}} = \frac{5}{{13}} \end{aligned}$$ We have seen that $$\sin \left( a \right) = \frac{5}{{13}}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{AB}}{{AE}} = \frac{5}{{13}} \\ & \Rightarrow AE = AB \times \frac{{13}}{5} \\ & = 250 \times \frac{{13}}{5} \\ & = 650\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e., Distance between the top of the buildings = 650 m

q: From a tower of 80 m high, the angle of depression of a bus is 30°. How far is the bus from the tower?
s: Let AC be the tower and B be the position of the bus. Then BC = the distance of the bus from the foot of the tower. Given that height of the tower, AC = 80 m and the angle of depression, ∠DAB = 30° ∠ABC = ∠DAB = 30° (because DA || BC) $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AC}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{80}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow BC = \frac{{80}}{{\tan {{30}^ \circ }}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{80}}{{\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)}} \\ & = 80 \times 1.73 = 138.4\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e., Distance of the bus from the foot of the tower = 138.4 m

q: The elevation of the summit of a mountain from its foot is 45°. After ascending 2 km towards the mountain upon an incline of 30°,the elevation changes to 60°. What is the approximate height of the mountain?
s: Let A be the foot and C be the summit of a mountain. Given that ∠CAB = 45° From the diagram, CB is the height of the mountain. Let CB = x Let D be the point after ascending 2 km towards the mountain such that AD = 2 km and given that ∠DAY = 30° It is also given that from the point D, the elevation is 60° i.e., ∠CDE = 60° $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta ABC, \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{CB}}{{AB}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow 1 = \frac{x}{{AB}}$$ [n CB = x(the height of the mountain)] $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow AB = x\,......\left( 1 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta AYD, \\ & \sin {30^ \circ } = \frac{{DY}}{{AD}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} = \frac{{DY}}{2}$$ (n Given that AD = 2) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow DY = 1\,.......\left( 2 \right) \\ & \cos {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AY}}{{AD}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} = \frac{{AY}}{2}$$ (n Given that AD = 2) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow AY = \sqrt 3 \,......\left( 3 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta CED, \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{CE}}{{DE}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{\left( {CB - EB} \right)}}{{YB}}$$ [n CE = (CB - EB) and DE = YB)] $$\Rightarrow \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{\left( {CB - DY} \right)}}{{AB - AY}}$$ [n EB = DY and YB = (AB - AY)] $$\Rightarrow \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{\left( {x - 1} \right)}}{{\left( {x - \sqrt 3 } \right)}}$$ [n CB = x, DY = 1(eq:2), AB = x(eq:1) and AY = $${\sqrt 3 }$$ (eq:3)] $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{{\left( {x - 1} \right)}}{{\left( {x - \sqrt 3 } \right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow x\sqrt 3 - 3 = x - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow x\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) = 2 \\ & \Rightarrow 0.73x = 2 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{2}{{0.73}} = 2.7 \end{aligned}$$ i.e., the height of the mountain = 2.7 km

q: A flagstaff is placed on top of a building. The flagstaff and building subtend equal angles at a point on level ground which is 200 m away from the foot of the building. If the height of the flagstaff is 50 m and the height of the building is h, which of the following is true?
s: Let AD be the flagstaff and CD be the building. Assume that the flagstaff and building subtend equal angles at point B. Given that AD = 50 m, CD = h and BC = 200 m Let ∠ABD = $$\theta$$, ∠DBC = $$\theta$$ (n flagstaff and building subtend equal angles at a point on level ground). Then, ∠ABC = 2$$\theta$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta BCD, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{DC}}{{BC}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{h}{{200}}\,......\left( 1 \right) \\ & {\text{From}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{right}}\,\Delta BCA, \\ & \tan 2\theta = \frac{{AC}}{{BC}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{AD + DC}}{{200}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50 + h}}{{200}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{{2\tan \theta }}{{1 - {{\tan }^2}\theta }} = \frac{{50 + h}}{{200}}$$ $$\left( {\because \tan \left( {2\theta } \right) = \frac{{2\tan \theta }}{{1 - {{\tan }^2}\theta }}} \right)$$ $$\frac{{2\left( {\frac{h}{{200}}} \right)}}{{1 - \frac{{{h^2}}}{{{{200}^2}}}}} = \frac{{50 + h}}{{200}}$$ (n substituted value of tan $$\theta$$ from eq:1) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2h = \left( {1 - \frac{{{h^2}}}{{{{200}^2}}}} \right)\,\left( {50 + h} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 2h = 50 + h - \frac{{50{h^2}}}{{{{200}^2}}} - \frac{{{h^3}}}{{{{200}^2}}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow 2\left( {{{200}^2}} \right)h = 50{\left( {200} \right)^2} +$$ $$h{\left( {200} \right)^2} -$$ $$50{h^2} - {h^3}$$ (n multiplied LHS and RHS by $${{{200}^2}}$$ ) h 3 + 50h 2 + (200) 2 h - (200) 2 50 = 0

q: From the top of a hill 100 m high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a pole are 30° and 60° respectively. What is the height of the pole?
s: Consider the diagram shown above. AC represents the hill and DE represents the pole Given that AC = 100 m ∠XAD = ∠ADB = 30° (n AX || BD ) ∠XAE = ∠AEC = 60° (n AX || CE) Let DE = h Then, BC = DE = h, AB = (100 - h) (n AC = 100 and BC = h), BD = CE $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{AC}}{{CE}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt 3 = \frac{{100}}{{CE}} \\ & \Rightarrow CE = \frac{{100}}{{\sqrt 3 }}\,......\left( 1 \right) \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BD}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{100 - h}}{{BD}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{100 - h}}{{\left( {\frac{{100}}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)}}$$ (n BD = CE and substituted the value of CE from eq. 1) $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \left( {100 - h} \right) = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} \times \frac{{100}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{100}}{3} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 33.33 \\ & \Rightarrow h = 100 - 33.33 = 66.67\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ i.e., the height of the pole = 66.67 m

q: A poster is on top of a building. Rajesh is standing on the ground at a distance of 50 m from the building. The angles of elevation to the top of the poster and bottom of the poster are 45° and 30° respectively. What is the height of the poster?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{in}}\,\Delta PNQ,\,\tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{PQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \therefore PQ = NQ = 50{\text{m}} \\ & {\text{in}}\,\Delta MNQ,\,\tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{MQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{MQ}}{{50}} \\ & \therefore MQ = \frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \therefore h = PM \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = PQ - MQ \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 50 - \frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }}\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right) \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Poster height = $$\frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }}\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)$$

q: Angles of elevation of pole are 60° and 45° from points at distances m and n on ground respectively. Here m, when measured from base of pole is less than n. What is the height of the pole?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Height}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{pole}} = PQ \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \sqrt 3 = \frac{{PQ}}{m} \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = 1 = \frac{{PQ}}{n} \\ & {\text{Multiply}}\,{\text{both}}\,{\text{equations}} \\ & \sqrt 3 \times 1 = \frac{{PQ}}{m} \times \frac{{PQ}}{n} \\ & \therefore PQ = \sqrt {mn\sqrt 3 } \,{\text{units}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tree is cut partially and made to fall on ground. The tree however does not fall completely and is still attached to its cut part. The tree top touches the ground at a point 10m from foot of the tree making an angle of 30°. What is the length of the tree?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{in}}\,\Delta MNQ,\tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{MQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{MQ}}{{10}} \\ & \therefore MQ = \frac{{10}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & {\text{Also}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{Pythagoras}}\,{\text{theorem}} \\ & M{N^2} = M{Q^2} + N{Q^2} \\ & \therefore {L^2} = \frac{{100}}{3} + 100 \\ & \therefore L = \frac{{20}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \therefore {\text{Height}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{tree}} \\ & = L + MQ \\ & = \frac{{20}}{{\sqrt 3 }} + \frac{{10}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = \frac{{30}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = \frac{{3 \times 10}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = 10\sqrt 3 \,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Tree top’s angle of elevation is 30° from a point on ground, 300m away the tree. When the tree grew up its angle of elevation became 60° from the same point. How much did the tree grow?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Original tree height}} = {\text{h}} = {\text{MQ}} \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{tree}}\,{\text{height}} = PQ \\ & {\text{in}}\,\Delta MQN,\,\tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{MQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \therefore MQ = \frac{{300}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & {\text{in}}\,\Delta PQN,\,\tan {60^ \circ } = \sqrt 3 = \frac{{PQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \therefore PQ = 300\sqrt 3 \\ & {\text{Tree}}\,{\text{grew}} = PQ - MQ \\ & \therefore {\text{Tree}}\,{\text{grew}} \\ & = 300\sqrt 3 - \frac{{300}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = 300\frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = 3 \times 100 \times \frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = 200\sqrt 3 \,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Mohan looks at a tree top and the angle made is 45°. He moves 10 cm back and again looks at the tree top but this time angle made is 30°. How high is the tree top from ground?
s: Let PQ be three and M and N be positions where Mphan stands. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now,}}\,{\text{tan}}{45^ \circ } = 1 = \frac{{PQ}}{{MQ}} \\ & \therefore PQ = MQ \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{PQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{PQ}}{{10 + MQ}} \\ & \therefore 10 + MQ = \sqrt 3 \,PQ \end{aligned}$$ $$\therefore 10 + PQ = \sqrt 3 \,PQ$$ (As, PQ = MQ) $$\therefore PQ = \frac{{10}}{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}\,{\text{cm}}$$

q: Rohit while seeing a bird on tree top made 45° angle of elevation. He walks 240ft. towards the tree to observe the bird closely, thus making 60° angle of elevation. How far was Rohit from the tree initially?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Now,}}\,{\text{tan}}{45^ \circ } = 1 = \frac{{PQ}}{{NQ}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Tree}}\,{\text{height}} \\ & = PQ = NQ \\ & = \left( {240 + MQ} \right) \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \sqrt 3 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{PQ}}{{MQ}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{240 + MQ}}{{MQ}} \\ & \therefore 240 + MQ = \sqrt 3 \,MQ \\ & \therefore MQ = \frac{{240}}{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}\,{\text{ft}} \\ & \therefore NQ = 240 + MQ \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{240\sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}\,{\text{ft}} \end{aligned}$$ = Rohit was this much far away initially

q: A tree breaks and falls to the ground such that its upper part is still partially attached to its stem. At what height did it break, if the original height of the tree was 24 cm and it makes an angle of 30° with the ground?
s: Let the tree break at height h cm from ground at point M. The broken part makes angle of 30° ∴ Broken Part MP = MN = 24 - h $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{in}}\,\Delta MCQ, \\ & \sin {30^ \circ } = \frac{1}{2} = \frac{{MQ}}{{MN}} = \frac{{\text{h}}}{{24 - {\text{h}}}} \\ & \therefore 24 - {\text{h}} = 2{\text{h}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ h = 8 cm = Tree breaks at this height

q: Two houses are in front of each other. Both have chimneys on their top. The line joining the chimneys makes an angle of 45° with the ground. How far are the houses from each other if one house is 25m and other is 10m in height?
s: In ∠ABR, ∠ARB = 90° and ∠BAR = 45° Sum of angles of a triangle = 180° So ∠ABR = 180 - 90 - 45 = 45° ∴ BR = AR AS = RQ = 10m Also, BR = BQ - RQ = 25 - 10 = 15m ∴ AR = 15m = Distance between houses

q: Shadow of a man is $$\frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}$$ times the height of the man. What will be the sun’s angle of elevation?
s: Shadow length = $$\frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}$$ Height of man $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{{\text{Height}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{man}}}}{{{\text{Shadow}}\,{\text{length}}}} = \sqrt 3 \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{{\text{Height}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{man}}}}{{{\text{Shadow}}\,{\text{length}}}} = \sqrt 3 \\ & {\text{But}}\,\tan {60^ \circ } = \sqrt 3 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ $$\theta$$ = 60° = Angle of elevation of sum

q: There is a tree between houses of A and B. If the tree leans on A’s House, the tree top rests on his window which is 12 m from ground. If the tree leans on B’s House, the tree top rests on his window which is 9 m from ground. If the height of the tree is 15 m, what is distance between A’s and B’s house?
s: In $$\Delta$$STR, by Pythagoras theorem $$\begin{aligned} & R{T^2} = S{T^2} + R{S^2} \\ & \therefore S{T^2} = {15^2} - {9^2} = 144 \\ & \therefore ST = 12\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ In $$\Delta$$TQP, by Pythagoras theorem $$\begin{aligned} & P{T^2} = T{Q^2} + P{Q^2} \\ & \therefore T{Q^2} = {15^2} - {12^2} = 81 \\ & \therefore TQ = 9\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ Distance between houses ⇒ SQ = ST + TQ ⇒ SQ = 12 + 9 ⇒ SQ = 21 m

q: Ramesh and Suresh’s mud forts have heights 8 cm and 15 cm. They are 24 cm apart. How far are the fort tops from each other?
s: Let MN = Ramesh's fort & PQ = Suresh's fort From the diagram we can see that MR = 24 cm & PR = 15 - 8 = 7 cm By Pythagoras theorem, Hypotenuse 2 = (side1) 2 + (side2) 2 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{MP}} = \sqrt {{{24}^2} + {7^2}} \\ & \therefore {\text{MP}} = 25\,{\text{cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A and B are standing on ground 50 meters apart. The angles of elevation for these two to the top of a tree are 60° and 30°. What is height of the tree?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{In}}\,\Delta PBQ,\,\tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{PQ}}{{BQ}} \\ & \therefore BQ = \frac{{PQ}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & {\text{In}}\,\Delta PAQ,\,\tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{PQ}}{{AQ}} \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{PQ}}{{50 + BQ}} \\ & \therefore PQ = \frac{{50 + BQ}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50 + \frac{{PQ}}{{\sqrt 3 }}}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50\sqrt 3 + PQ}}{{\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 }} \\ & \therefore 3PQ = 50\sqrt 3 + PQ \end{aligned}$$ $$\therefore PQ = 25\sqrt 3 \,{\text{m}} =$$ Height of tree

q: There is a tower of 10m between two parallel roads. The angles of depression of the roads from the top of the tower are 30° and 45°. How far are the roads from each other?
s: Angle of Depression = Angle of Elevation Tower PS = 10 m in height $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{tan}}{45^ \circ } = 1 = \frac{{PS}}{{RS}} \\ & \therefore PS = RS = 10 \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{PS}}{{SQ}} = \frac{{10}}{{SQ}} \\ & \therefore SQ = 10\sqrt 3 \\ & RQ = RS + SQ \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 10 + 10\sqrt 3 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 27.32\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Raj stands in a corner of his square farm. Angle of elevation of a scarecrow placed in diagonally opposite corner is 60°. He starts walking backwards in a straight line and after 80ft he realizes that angle of elevation of the scarecrow now is 30°. What is area of the field?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {60^ \circ } = \sqrt 3 = \frac{{PQ}}{{QR}} \\ & \therefore PQ = \sqrt 3 \,QR \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{PQ}}{{SQ}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{PQ}}{{80 + QR}} \\ & \therefore 80 + QR = \sqrt 3 \,PQ \\ & \therefore 80 + QR = 3QR \\ & \therefore QR = 40\,{\text{ft}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$ If we read carefully, we see that Raj (Point R) and the scarecrow (Point Q) are in diagonally opposite corners. So QR is a diagonal of the square farm. Diagonal of square = side x$$\sqrt 2$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 40 = {\text{side}}\,{\text{x}}\sqrt 2 \\ & \therefore {\text{side}} = \frac{{40}}{{\sqrt 2 }} \\ & \therefore {\text{Area}} = {\left( {{\text{side}}} \right)^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\left( {\frac{{40}}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {\frac{{1600}}{2}} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 800\,{\text{sq}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{ft}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Due to sun, a 6ft man casts a shadow of 4ft, whereas a pole next to the man casts a shadow of 36ft. What is the height of the pole?
s: Both the man and pole are near each other and are illuminated by same sun from same direction. So angle of elevation for sun is same for both. So ration of object to shadow will be same for all objects. (Proportionality Rule) $$\frac{{{\text{Object}}\,{\text{height}}}}{{{\text{Shadow}}\,{\text{length}}}} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{{\text{H}}}{{36}}$$ ∴ H = 54 ft = Height of pole

q: From the top of a hill 200 m high the angle of depression of the top and the bottom of a tower are observed to be 30° and 60°. The height of the tower is (in m);
s: $$\begin{aligned} & AB = {\text{hill}} = 200{\text{ metre}} \\ & CD = {\text{tower}} \\ & {\text{In }}\Delta \,APC \\ & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{AP}}{{PC}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{AP}}{{PC}} \\ & \Rightarrow AP:PC = 1:\sqrt 3 \,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{In }}\Delta \,ABD \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BD}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{AB}}{{BD}} \\ & \Rightarrow AB:BD = \sqrt 3 :1\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & PB = CD{\text{ and }}PC = BD \\ & {\text{Now}} \end{aligned}$$ \[\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {AB}&:&{BD}&:&{AP} \\ {\sqrt 3 }&:&1&{}&{} \\ {}&{}&{\sqrt 3 }&:&1 \\ 3&:&{\sqrt 3 }&:&1 \end{array}\] $$\begin{aligned} & CD = PB \Rightarrow AB - AP \\ & CD = 3 - 1 \\ & CD = 2{\text{ units}} \\ & AB = 3{\text{ units}} = 200{\text{ metre}} \\ & CD = 2{\text{ units}} = \frac{{200}}{3} \times 2 = 133\frac{1}{3}\,{\text{metre}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The angle of elevation of an aeroplane as observed from a point 30 m above the transport water-surface of lake is 30° and the angle of depression of the image of the aeroplane in the water of the lake is 60°. The height of the aeroplane from the water-surface of the lake is

q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tall building from the points M and N at the distances of 72 m and 128 m, respectively, from the base of building and in the same straight line with it, are complementary. The height of the building (in m) is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{In }}\Delta ABM, \\ & \tan \left( {90 - \theta } \right) = \frac{P}{B} = \frac{{AB}}{{72}} \\ & \frac{1}{{\cot \theta }} = \frac{{72}}{{AB}} \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{{72}}{{AB}}{\text{ }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{In }}\Delta ABN, \\ & \tan \theta = \frac{P}{B} = \frac{{AB}}{{128}}{\text{ }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{From equation }}\left( {\text{i}} \right){\text{ and }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & \frac{{72}}{{AB}} = \frac{{AB}}{{128}} \\ & A{B^2} = 128 \times 72 \\ & AB = \sqrt {16 \times 4 \times 2 \times 36 \times 2} \\ & AB = 4 \times 4 \times 6 \\ & AB = 96 \end{aligned}$$

q: The distance between two parallel poles is 40√3 m. The angle of depression of the top of the second pole when seen from the top of first pole is 30°. What will be the height of second tower if the first pole is 100 m long

q: P and Q are two points on the ground on either side of a pole. The angles of elevation of the top of the pole as observed from P and Q are 60° and 30°, respectively and the distance between them is 84√3 m. What is the height (in m) of the pole?
s: \[{60^ \circ } = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{1}\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} \to &h \\ \to &{\frac{h}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \end{array}\] $$PN = \frac{h}{{\sqrt 3 }}$$ \[{30^ \circ } = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} \to &h \\ \to &{\sqrt 3 h} \end{array}\] $$\begin{aligned} & NQ = \sqrt 3 h \\ & PN + NQ = 84\sqrt 3 \\ & \frac{h}{{\sqrt 3 }} + \sqrt 3 h = 84\sqrt 3 \\ & h\left( {1 + 3} \right) = 84 \times \sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 \\ & h = \frac{{84 \times 3}}{4} \\ & h = 63\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A ladder is placed along a wall such that its upper end is touching the top of the wall. The foot of the ladder is 10 ft away from the wall and the ladder is making an angle of 60° with the ground. When a man starts climbing on it, it slips and now ladder makes an angle of 30° with ground. How much did the ladder slip?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & AB = 10\tan {60^ \circ } = 10\sqrt 3 \\ & BC = 10\sec {60^ \circ } = 20 \end{aligned}$$ Since, length of ladder will remain same, hence BC = DE = 20 $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{In }}\Delta ADE,\,DE = 20{\text{ ft}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{AD}}{{DE}} = \cos {30^ \circ } \\ & \Rightarrow AD = 20 \times \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} = 10\sqrt 3 \\ & \Rightarrow x = AD - AC \\ & \Rightarrow x = 10\sqrt 3 - 10 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 10\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right){\text{ft}} \end{aligned}$$

q: From the top of a 12 m high building, The angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 60° and the angle of depression of the foot of the tower is θ. Such that tan θ = $$\frac{3}{4}$$, what is the height of the tower (√3 = 1.73)?
s: Let AB be the building and EC be the tower. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{In }}\Delta ADE \\ & \tan {60^ \circ } = \frac{{ED}}{{AD}} \\ & \sqrt 3 = \frac{{ED}}{{16}} \\ & ED = 16\sqrt 3 = 16 \times 1.73 = 27.68\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$ Hence the height of the tower EC = CD + ED = 12 + 27.68 = 39.68 m

q: A poster is on top of a building. A person is standing on the ground at a distance of 50 m from the building. The angles of elevation to the top of the poster and bottom of the poster are 45° and 30°, respectively. What is 200% of the height (in cm) of the poster?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \tan {30^ \circ } = \frac{{BD}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} = \frac{{BD}}{{50}} \\ & \Rightarrow BD = \frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \tan {45^ \circ } = \frac{{AB}}{{BC}} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 = \frac{{AB}}{{50}} \\ & \Rightarrow AB = 50 \\ & \therefore AD = AB - BD \\ & = 50 - \frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = \frac{{50\left( {\sqrt 3 - 1} \right)\sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 3 \times \sqrt 3 }} \\ & = \frac{{50}}{3}\left( {3 - \sqrt 3 } \right){\text{m}} \\ & 200\% {\text{ of }}AD = \frac{{50}}{3}\left( {3 - \sqrt 3 } \right) \times \frac{{200}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{100}}{3}\left( {3 - \sqrt 3 } \right){\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$
